text_blocks.snippet: To file a roof insurance claim in Utah, [Highlight start] note the date of the storm, document visible damage safely from the ground, get a professional roof inspection, and report the claim promptly to your homeowners insurer [Highlight end] .
snippet_highlighted_words: [Highlight start] note the date of the storm, document visible damage safely from the ground, get a professional roof inspection, and report the claim promptly to your homeowners insurer [Highlight end]

list.snippet: Note the storm date and check your policy: Record when the wind, hail, or snow event happened. Review your deductible (often $500–$2,000), coverage terms (such as actual cash value vs. replacement cost), and filing deadlines.

Document visible damage safely: Take photos and videos of missing or lifted shingles, dented vents/flashing, hailstones, fallen branches, or granules in gutters from the ground. Avoid climbing onto a steep, wet, or damaged roof.
Make emergency temporary repairs if needed: If water is entering your home, tarping or stabilizing the leak helps prevent further damage. Keep all receipts and photos of emergency work.

Get a licensed roofer inspection: Have a licensed Utah roofing contractor inspect the roof for storm damage (like hail bruising or lifted shingles) versus normal wear and tear or age. Ask for a written report and photos.
File the claim with your insurer: Contact your insurance company or agent to open the claim, get a claim number, and schedule an adjuster visit. Keep a log of dates, names, and call notes.

Meet the insurance adjuster: Be present for the inspection—and consider having your contractor there—so storm-related damage isn't missed. Settlements often take roughly 30 to 60 days depending on claim volume and scope.

Review the estimate and complete repairs: Compare the insurer's scope and payout against your roofer's estimate. If valid storm damage or code items are missing, your contractor can submit a supplement/estimate review to the adjuster.
